text.tspan: Supplemental Figure 3. Estimated normalized terminal velocity species and PC1 distributions.The x axes are mean-normalized terminal
velocity computed under a Stokes-flow approximation for prolate spheroids, assuming the highest-drag orientation (long axis parallel to the
ground or “broadside” settling). Values are normalized by the across-species mean (dashed vertical line at 1.0). (A) Number of species with
each relative settling velocity. There is an approximate 5x difference between the extremes. (B) Shows the relationship between species
mean PC1 and relative settling velocity. The solid line is the least-squares fit and the shaded band is the 95% confidence interval for the
mean fitted relationship; Pearson r and R² are reported in-panel. This analysis is intended as a comparative, dimensionless proxy rather
than an estimate of absolute terminal velocity: shared physical constants (e.g., density contrast, gravitational acceleration, air viscosity) are
omitted, and orientation is fixed to maximize drag; real spores may depart from the ellipsoidal model and experience slip correction,
turbulence, boundary-layer effects, and variable orientations.
